Kids settings vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Kids workflow covers language. Connect actually separates compliance flags from storefront copy:

  • Kids category / Made for Kids — affects review rules, ad behavior, external links, and age-band targeting. You set this during submission or in App Information. It does not generate Chinese text.
  • Age rating questionnaire — produces the age band Apple displays. Answering in English does not populate zh-Hans name, subtitle, or description fields.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Kids flags.

A compliant US Kids listing and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

Parents and educators browsing the China App Store evaluate age fit in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

Kids-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Kids app listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese parents and teachers describe age bands and learning goals — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Age-band phrasing

US pages use "Ages 5+", "Preschool", or "Grades K–2". China storefront copy often uses 幼儿, 学龄前, 3–6岁, or 小学 — depending on your actual age rating band. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your Connect age rating, not inventing a different band.

Educational benefit lines

Screenshot overlays and description leads reference outcomes — literacy, numeracy, creativity, social-emotional skills. Chinese parents expect concrete outcomes (识字, 拼音, 逻辑思维) rather than English edu-marketing slogans ("brain boost", "future-ready").

Safety and trust tone

Kids listings often mention ad-free play, no external links, or offline mode. These are factual product claims in description copy — not substitutes for privacy-policy legal text, which AppLocale does not write.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Kids-relevant search terms Chinese caregivers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Genre nouns differ from game or productivity apps: 儿童教育, 绘本, 儿歌, 早教 each signal different intent.

Common mistakes on Kids app zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Made for Kids localizes automatically — compliance flag set; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US "For Kids" badges verbatim — Latin badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Pasting US curriculum names without context — "Common Core" and state standards do not land the same way for China readers unless your app actually targets that curriculum
  • Utility-app tone on a Kids product — "productivity", "workflow", or "AI-powered" phrasing copied from a non-Kids template
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Conflating listing copy with privacy compliance — description mentions COPPA or GDPR instead of parent-readable product facts; legal policy text belongs in your privacy URL, not AppLocale scope
  • Expecting AppLocale to fix Kids review rejections — incomplete metadata may cause review issues, but category application, parental-gate implementation, and ad network configuration are outside listing rewrite
